figures.caption: Figure 5: Case A4. Scope boundary enforcement on a numeric threshold query. The system correctly reports no validated cut-off and cites three sources. The source panel confirms that none of the retrieved chunks contains a numeric threshold.
Table 1: MECFS-KB source composition. IQWiG N21-01 chunks are annotated as conflicting with NICE NG206.

Figure 2: Case A1. GET conflict query in clinician mode. The response cites CCC 2003 [6] and NICE NG206 [31], flags the conflict with IQWiG N21-01 [14], and recommends individualised activity pacing. The source panel shows the two retrieved guideline chunks.

Figure 4: Case A3. CBT conflict query in clinician mode. The response presents the NICE NG206 [31] and IQWiG N21-01 [14] disagreement with source attribution. Three retrieved chunks are shown in the right panel.

Figure 1: Overview of knowledge base and ARCagent construction. (a) Knowledge base construction: sources are collected and chunked into guideline, empirical, genomic, and observational knowledge, with a conflict registry annotating conflict zones. (b) ARCagent construction: a query is processed into a focus profile, resolved through conflict-aware retrieval, and answered via dual-mode response generation.

Figure 7: Case A6. Same disease naming query as Case A5 in patient mode. The same three sources are retrieved but the response uses plain language and omits guideline version specifics. Comparing A5 and A6 directly illustrates the dual-mode register shift.

Table 3: Comparison of three scoring methods. LLM refers to automated LLM-as-Judge scoring with llama3.1-8b. Keyword refers to keyword matching. Human refers to blinded ratings by three medical graduate student raters. The Δ row shows per-column deviation from the Human-as-Judge average.

Table 2: Full benchmark results. Auto denotes autonomic dysfunction and comorbidity queries. Diag denotes diagnostic criteria queries. Navi denotes care-navigation queries. PEM denotes post-exertional malaise management queries. Scop denotes out-of-scope refusal queries. Conf denotes inter-guideline conflict queries. Spec denotes guideline-specific detail queries. RevH denotes revision history queries. The lower block shows domain-specific medical LLMs. The ARCagent rows compare retrieval-first and adaptive retrieval calibration variants. Bold indicates per-category best.

Figure 6: Case A5. Disease naming query in clinician mode. Six sources are retrieved. The response addresses historical, geographic, and diagnostic significance of naming differences using clinical framing.

Figure 3: Case A2. Diagnostic criteria conflict in clinician mode. Four sources are retrieved and two inter-framework disagreements are surfaced. The source panel shows retrieved chunks from IOM 2015 [15], ICC 2012 [7], and CCC 2003 [6].

Table 4: Unified knowledge ablation using Grok-4.20 base model. The upper block removes one knowledge type and the lower block removes one guideline source category. Column labels match Table 2. Full KB row shows the baseline. All values are LLM-as-Judge scores reported as percentages without the percent symbol.

Table 5: Qualitative comparison on the GET conflict query in clinician mode. Grok-4.20 without retrieval generates a response that does not surface the NICE NG206 prohibition or flag any inter-guideline disagreement. ARCagent detects the conflict intent, retrieves passages from both NICE NG206 and IQWiG N21-01, and presents both stances with inline source attribution.
